title: The orders report melts under real data
summary: The report was built against a test database with a dozen orders in it. It went out to a customer with four thousand and took most of a minute. Same figures when you are done, in the same shape.

checkpoints.title: The report says the same thing it always did
checkpoints.hint: Every figure is checked against the same query written by hand. Making it fast and making it wrong is not an improvement.

checkpoints.title: It does not cost a query per order
checkpoints.hint: Count the statements for five orders and for sixty. If the two numbers differ, the loop is the problem: join the customer in rather than looking each one up.

checkpoints.title: The counting and adding up happen in the database
checkpoints.hint: Joining every line item into one query fixes the round trips and still ships thousands of rows to add up here. COUNT, SUM and GROUP BY give you a row per order instead.

checkpoints.title: An order with nothing on it still appears
checkpoints.hint: An inner join to the line items drops any order that has none. LEFT JOIN keeps it, and COALESCE turns the resulting NULL sum into a zero.
